name: Coffee
anchor: Per-form sovereign beverage cells in the as-consumed liquid basis (EU 2023/915 juice and rice-drink cells, Codex CXS 193 fruit juices, EU 2024/1987 beverage nickel, EU canned-beverage tin, Hong Kong Cap 132V's named carbonated, tea, coffee and wine beverage entries, and the US and Hong Kong packaged-drinking-water quality standards), with dry leaf, bean and powder commodities anchored separately in their own as-sold basis and never converted between the two
native_basis_label: dry commodity as sold (green beans, roasted whole beans, ground coffee, coffee pods and capsules assessed on their coffee fill, instant coffee solids), reported on the as-sold article; this is the lot the applicant packages and the auditor samples
scope_note: Coffee as a dry commodity: green and roasted Coffea arabica and canephora beans, ground coffee, single-serve pods and capsules assessed on the coffee fill rather than the hardware, and instant or freeze-dried coffee solids. A mushroom coffee or any coffee carrying a Supplement Facts panel routes to Category 16 by the taxonomy boundary rule. Coffee-flavoured dairy and plant beverages route to Category 24 or the plant-milk rows respectively. Hong Kong Cap 132V writes the product-form split for this commodity itself, setting Coffee beans at 500 ug/kg lead in the as-sold basis and Coffee beverages at 200 ug/kg in the as-consumed basis under its Note 11; HMTc preserves the split. An applicant selling canned or bottled ready-to-drink coffee is assessed on that product form in the as-consumed liquid basis against the 200 ug/kg beverage cell; an applicant selling beans, grounds, pods or instant solids is assessed in this row's dry basis. Neither number is converted into the other basis, and no brew-strength or extraction factor is invented in either direction. The capsule or pod hardware itself is a food-contact article and is governed by Category 9, not here.
basis_guard: as[ _]sold|product as placed on market|edible part|dry matter|dry weight
basis_guard_note: This row publishes a dry-commodity ceiling in the as-sold basis (the article the applicant packages and the lot the auditor samples), so every named anchor must itself be a dry-commodity as-sold or as-placed-on-market cell. The guard refuses the ready-to-drink beverage cells: Hong Kong Cap 132V Note 11 restricts its beverage entries to beverages that are, or are reconstituted to be, ready to drink, and applying a ready-to-drink ceiling to a dry leaf, bean or powder would be a basis conflation in the strict direction, not a standard.
method: HMTc Method v2.0 (government-limit-only): the strictest applicable sovereign maximum level for this exact beverage form and analyte in the row's declared native basis, with disclosed read-across where the exact cell is unregulated, a substantiated not-material determination where a species is bounded or is a method artifact, and a control where no defensible sovereign number and no supportable near-neighbour exist. Never occurrence-derived. Ready-to-drink and dry-commodity bases are never mixed and no brewing, dilution or reconstitution factor is invented.

Pb.label: Lead 500 ug/kg is the strictest sovereign coffee maximum level in the as-sold dry basis, set concurrently by Hong Kong Cap 132V (coffee beans, 0.5 mg/kg), MERCOSUR GMC Res 12/2011 (roasted coffee beans and powder, 0.5 mg/kg) and Paraguay Decreto 1335/2019 (the identical MERCOSUR transposition). A single coffee row certifies every dry form against this strictest applicable value.
Pb.substantiation: Direct regulatory lookup. Three sovereigns converge on 500 ug/kg for the roasted bean and powder on the as-sold basis, and HMTc applies that ceiling across the dry coffee forms in scope (green bean, roasted bean, ground, pod fill, instant solids), because roasting and grinding are physical transformations of the same commodity that do not add lead and instant solids concentrate the extractable fraction of a bean already held to this ceiling. That single-commodity extension is disclosed, and it over-complies relative to the looser government-written soluble-coffee cells (MERCOSUR and Paraguay both 1000 ug/kg), Singapore coffee beans (2000) and Vietnam coffee (2000), each recorded here rather than buried. The Thailand residual food-other lead cell (1000, as-sold) also legally reaches coffee but is looser and is surveyed, not selected. China GB 2762-2022 is register-verified to exclude raw and roasted coffee beans from its nuts-and-seeds lead cell, so it sets no coffee lead limit. Hong Kong caps the resulting ready-to-drink coffee beverage at 200 ug/kg as consumed; that product-form split is preserved rather than collapsed into this dry-commodity row. Occurrence data played no part.

Cd.label: Cadmium 100 ug/kg is the strictest sovereign coffee maximum level in the as-sold dry basis, set by MERCOSUR GMC Res 12/2011 (roasted coffee beans and powder, 0.1 mg/kg) and its identical Paraguay Decreto 1335/2019 transposition.
Cd.substantiation: Direct regulatory lookup. The roasted bean and powder cadmium cell at 100 ug/kg is the strictest admissible as-sold coffee value and binds the harmonized dry row, over-complying relative to the government-written soluble-coffee cells (MERCOSUR and Paraguay both 200) and Vietnam coffee (1000). No general as-sold cadmium cell in the register is stricter: Singapore other-food and Uruguay solid-foods both sit at 200. The EU, Codex, FSANZ and Health Canada set no cadmium maximum level for coffee in any form. Register-sourced, not occurrence-derived.

tAs.label: Total arsenic 200 ug/kg is the strictest sovereign coffee maximum level in the as-sold dry basis, set by MERCOSUR GMC Res 12/2011 (roasted coffee beans and powder, 0.2 mg/kg) and its identical Paraguay Decreto 1335/2019 transposition. It also serves as the enforceable parent ceiling for the inorganic-arsenic species bound.
tAs.substantiation: Direct regulatory lookup. The MERCOSUR and Paraguay total-arsenic roasted bean and powder cell at 200 ug/kg is the strictest admissible as-sold coffee value and binds the harmonized row, over-complying relative to the soluble-coffee cells (both 500), Singapore coffee beans (1000), Vietnam coffee (1000) and the Thailand residual food-other total-arsenic cell (2000). The regulators that write beverage arsenic limits on the inorganic species (EU fruit juices, US FDA apple juice) do not reach coffee. Total arsenic is the parent screen that gates reflex inorganic-arsenic speciation. Register-sourced, not occurrence-derived.

iAs.rationale: No sovereign sets an inorganic-arsenic maximum level for coffee, and coffee is not a defining-inorganic-arsenic-pathway matrix carrying a species-only limit (unlike rice or apple juice). Under the Certification-Readiness Ruling's species-bounding clause, inorganic arsenic is a component of total arsenic bounded by the total-arsenic ceiling adjudicated for this row (iAs <= tAs = 200 ug/kg), an enforceable ceiling via reflex speciation rather than an empty cell or a fabricated number.
iAs.reference_method: Inorganic arsenic by HPLC-ICP-MS, reflexed whenever total arsenic on the lot reaches the trigger min(species limit, 50 percent of the total-arsenic ceiling); a confirmed result escalates to an origin and irrigation-water investigation. Inorganic arsenic never substitutes for the total-arsenic report.
iAs.regulatory_basis: No credible sovereign sets an inorganic-arsenic cell for coffee. Every sovereign inorganic-arsenic limit is scoped to rice and rice-based products, to a ready-to-drink beverage (EU fruit juices 20 ug/kg, EU non-alcoholic rice-based drinks 30 ug/kg, US FDA apple juice 10 ug/kg), to seafood, or to drinking water. Inorganic arsenic is a component of and bounded by total arsenic, which this row governs directly.
iAs.jurisdictions_checked: EU 2023/915; Codex CXS 193; US FDA (apple-juice action level, Closer to Zero); FSANZ Schedule 19; Health Canada; MERCOSUR GMC 12/2011; Paraguay Decreto 1335/2019; Singapore Food Regulations; Vietnam QCVN 8-2:2011; Thailand MOPH 414/2020 — none sets an inorganic-arsenic limit for coffee.
iAs.substantiation: Bounded by the total-arsenic cell (tAs = 200 ug/kg). Enforced by reflex speciation; not a routine per-lot species assay for this form.

tHg.label: Total mercury 20 ug/kg is the strictest applicable sovereign maximum level reaching coffee in the as-sold basis, set by Thailand MOPH Notification 414/2020 as the residual mercury cell for foods other than the listed mercury categories (0.02 mg/kg). Thailand sets no coffee-specific mercury cell, so coffee falls under this residual, which is stricter than and supersedes the looser coffee-specific Vietnam QCVN 8-2:2011 value (50 ug/kg).
tHg.substantiation: Direct regulatory lookup, register-verified. Method v2.0 selects the strictest applicable sovereign maximum level, and an already-admitted residual food-other total-mercury cell (Thailand MOPH 414/2020, as-sold) legally reaches dry coffee on the native basis and is stricter (20) than the Vietnam coffee-specific cell (50). If the Vietnam coffee cell is admissible then so is the Thailand food-other cell, and the stricter of the two binds. Singapore other-food and Uruguay foods-general both sit at 50 and are disclosed as looser. Mercury has no identified enrichment pathway in the coffee supply chain, but the analyte is on the mandatory eight-total panel and is measured every lot. Register-sourced, not occurrence-derived.

MeHg.rationale: Methylmercury has no formation pathway in dry coffee: there is no marine bioaccumulation step in the supply chain and no anaerobic, sulfate-reducing methylation environment in the product or its process. Methylmercury is a component of total mercury (MeHg <= tHg) and is governed by and bounded by the total-mercury ceiling adjudicated for this row (20 ug/kg); no separate methylmercury ceiling is published.
MeHg.reference_method: Bounded by the total-mercury cell (tHg = 20 ug/kg). Methylmercury speciation is reflexed only on an elevated total-mercury result; it is not a routine per-lot test for this form.
MeHg.regulatory_basis: No credible sovereign sets a methylmercury limit for any beverage, leaf, bean or beverage powder. Methylmercury maximum levels are scoped to fish, seafood and other marine matrices (EU 2023/915 section 3.3, US FDA CPG 540.600, Hong Kong Cap 132V fish entries). Methylmercury is a species of and bounded by total mercury, which this row governs directly.
MeHg.jurisdictions_checked: EU 2023/915; Codex CXS 193; US FDA; FSANZ Schedule 19; Health Canada; Hong Kong Cap 132V; MERCOSUR; Paraguay; Vietnam; Thailand — none sets a methylmercury limit for this product form.
MeHg.substantiation: Bounded by the total-mercury cell (tHg = 20 ug/kg). Enforced by reflex speciation.

Ni.source_scope: cocoa powder / fat-reduced cocoa powder (drinking chocolate)
Ni.label: Nickel 15000 ug/kg is a disclosed read-across from EU 2024/1987, which sets nickel in cocoa powder and fat-reduced cocoa powder (drinking chocolate) at 15 mg/kg. No sovereign sets a nickel maximum level for coffee; cocoa is the nearest applicable regulated commodity.
Ni.substantiation: Disclosed read-across, not direct governance. No sovereign regulates nickel in coffee. The nearest applicable sovereign cell is EU 2024/1987's cocoa-powder nickel limit (15000 ug/kg), and the analogy is agronomic rather than merely botanical: coffee and cocoa are the roasted seeds of tropical tree crops grown on acidic tropical soils that mobilise plant-available nickel, prepared and consumed as beverages, and cocoa powder is the closest processed analog to instant coffee solids. The EU assessed cocoa and set 15000 but did not assess coffee, so this value is applied by disclosed read-across and never presented as a coffee-specific government limit. The ceiling is a conservative backstop well above typical measured coffee nickel; nickel is a Tier-2 analyte measured every lot, and an elevated result escalates to a soil, cultivar and stainless-equipment investigation.

Sn.label: Tin 250000 ug/kg is set by the general food catch-all cells that legally reach coffee in the as-sold basis: Singapore Food Regulations Regulation 31(4) (any food, 250 ppm) and the Uruguay RBN foods-in-general cell (250 mg/kg). No sovereign writes a coffee-specific or dry-beverage-commodity tin cell; the canned and tinplate tin limits are container-migration cells in a different basis and are firewalled out of this dry row.
Sn.substantiation: Direct regulatory lookup against the general as-sold food catch-alls. Every product-specific tin limit in the register is a canned or tinplate container-migration cell written in a ready-to-drink or wet basis (the EU, Codex, MERCOSUR and Vietnam canned-beverage and canned-food cells, 100000 to 250000), and each excludes dried and powdered products by its own text; applying any of them to a dry commodity would be a basis conflation. The only sovereign tin numbers that reach dry coffee as sold are the general food catch-alls, which converge on 250000. Tin is a Tier-2 analyte with no raw-material source in coffee; an elevated result is a packaging-integrity signal, and where the applicant also sells a canned ready-to-drink coffee that form is verified separately against the canned-beverage tin cell in the as-consumed basis. Register-sourced, not occurrence-derived.

Al.rationale: No sovereign sets an aluminium maximum level for coffee, and no analogous dry-food aluminium contaminant cell exists: the only sovereign aluminium values are the packaged-drinking-water quality standards (a litre-of-water basis, Category 8) and the FSANZ infant-formula limits (Category 1), neither of which is applicable to a dry commodity, and Method v2.0 forbids deriving a ceiling from occurrence data. Aluminium nonetheless carries a real exposure pathway here (acidic tropical soils mobilise plant-available aluminium, and single-serve capsules are predominantly aluminium), so under the Certification-Readiness Ruling this cell is a baseline-monitor screen rather than a not-material determination. It is the one cell on this panel that cannot yet resolve to a firm limit-of-record: a testable numeric baseline of the form '< X ug/kg by ICP-MS' requires the accredited laboratory's documented method reporting limit, which is not yet in the register. Until that number is recorded the cell is a mandatory-monitored control and no ceiling is invented.
Al.reference_method: Total aluminium by ICP-MS on every certified lot, reported on the certificate in the as-sold dry basis, established as a baseline-monitor limit-of-record at the laboratory's documented reporting limit once provided. A result that departs materially from the applicant's documented origin and process baseline escalates to a soil, cultivar, capsule-packaging and processing-aid investigation. This is a process-control tripwire pending a documented method limit of quantification, not an invented numeric standard.

Cr.source_scope: grains and grain products including cereals and milled grain products
Cr.label: Total chromium 1000 ug/kg is a disclosed read-across from China GB 2762-2022, which sets total chromium uniformly at 1.0 mg/kg across its dry plant-food commodity classes (grains and grain products; beans, bean products and legumes). No sovereign sets a total-chromium maximum level for coffee; China GB 2762 is an already-admitted, live-cited HMTc anchor and the nearest applicable dry-plant-commodity instrument.
Cr.substantiation: Disclosed read-across, not direct governance. No sovereign regulates total chromium in coffee. China GB 2762-2022 sets a uniform total-chromium level of 1000 ug/kg across its dry plant-food commodity classes, and coffee is a dry plant-derived food commodity read across to that uniform level. Coffee is not itself a grain or a legume (it is the roasted seed of a tropical drupe), so the value is applied as a general dry-plant-commodity read-across rather than by claiming coffee into either China GB class; both the grains cell and the beans-and-legumes cell (identical at 1000) are named so the selection is auditable. Total chromium in this form is dominated by benign Cr(III) and is reported as a stainless-equipment and process-water leaching screen; the health-relevant species is governed in the Cr-VI cell. Register-sourced, not occurrence-derived.

Cr-VI.rationale: No sovereign sets a hexavalent-chromium limit for any food or beverage, and the in-matrix reduction argument that supports a not-material determination in an acidic aqueous beverage is unavailable here: this row's certified article is a dry bean, ground or solid with no aqueous phase in which Cr(VI) could reduce to Cr(III). Cr(VI) is a component of total chromium (Cr-VI <= total Cr) and is bounded by the total-chromium ceiling adjudicated for this row (1000 ug/kg), an enforceable ceiling via reflex speciation rather than an empty cell.
Cr-VI.reference_method: Total chromium by ICP-MS every lot; Cr(VI)-specific speciation (IC-ICP-MS, EN 15192 adapted) reflexed whenever total chromium reaches the trigger min(species limit, 50 percent of the total-chromium ceiling). A confirmed Cr(VI) detection escalates to a process-water, equipment and ingredient investigation and blocks certification pending resolution.
Cr-VI.regulatory_basis: No credible sovereign sets a hexavalent-chromium limit for any food or beverage. Cr(VI) is a component of and bounded by total chromium, which this row governs by read-across.
Cr-VI.jurisdictions_checked: EU 2023/915; Codex CXS 193; US FDA; FSANZ; Health Canada; China GB 2762-2022; Hong Kong Cap 132V — none sets a hexavalent-chromium limit for a food or beverage.
Cr-VI.substantiation: Bounded by the total-chromium cell (Cr = 1000 ug/kg). Enforced by reflex speciation.
